content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published a guideline on the use of ferritin concentrations to assess iron status in individuals and populations. This document provides evidence-based recommendations for the measurement and interpretation of ferritin levels, which are critical for diagnosing iron deficiency or overload and for guiding public health interventions. Ferritin is a protein that stores iron and is present in all cells. It can be measured in serum, plasma, liver, red blood cells, and other specimens. Low ferritin levels indicate depleted iron stores, while elevated levels may suggest iron overload. Accurate determination of iron status is essential for both clinical and public health purposes. In individual patients, diagnosing iron deficiency or overload helps guide further investigations and appropriate therapy. At the population level, assessing the prevalence and distribution of iron deficiency can help prioritize interventions in areas where it is a severe public health problem or identify populations at risk of hereditary conditions predisposing them to iron overload. The guideline outlines global recommendations for using ferritin concentrations to monitor and evaluate iron interventions. It is intended for a wide audience, including health professionals, clinicians, researchers, nutrition and health program managers, public health policymakers, and technical staff involved in designing and conducting micronutrient surveys. The development of this guideline followed rigorous procedures outlined in the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development. The process included identifying priority questions and outcomes, retrieving and synthesizing evidence, formulating recommendations, and planning for dissemination, implementation, and evaluation. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) methodology was used to prepare evidence profiles based on systematic reviews. The WHO acknowledges the contributions of various experts, technical advisors, and organizations in the development of this guideline. Financial support was provided by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Nutrition International, and the International Micronutrient Malnutrition Prevention and Control Program of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The WHO also receives grants from other donors, but these donors do not influence the guideline development process. This guideline updates and supersedes previous recommendations on ferritin use for assessing iron status, including those in the 2004 WHO/CDC publication Assessing the Iron Status of Populations and the 2001 guide Iron Deficiency Anaemia: Assessment, Prevention, and Control. It presents direct and indirect evidence, as well as qualitative reviews, to inform its recommendations.
